title: Documentation and the agents' context
headline: These costs are paid per agent session and grow with every feature built, not with shoppers, so the owner's clarification changes none of them. Every session and every subagent loads 44 KB (about 11,000 tokens, estimate at 4 characters a token); 71% of it is a 295-line index of which a typical change needs 2 to 4 lines, and taking it out saves about 29.5 KB (about 7,400 tokens) each time. What a search can show matters more than what is loaded: the harness's search tool prints nothing for a line over 500 characters, and such lines hold 98% of decisions.md and 52% of the rules, while source code has almost none (0.3%). Nothing caps any of it (CLAUDE.md regrew 35% in 12 days), and one cost the report missed is real work: sessions running at once take the same decision number, so 5 of 24 merges in 35 hours renumbered one, twice across 64 and 77 files.

findings.title: Every session loads a 295-line feature index; a typical change needs 2 to 4 of its lines
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md is 43,361 bytes and 448 lines. Its Storefront and Admin sections are 30,806 bytes (71%) in 305 lines: 295 one-line pointers, 28 cut with an ellipsis. The rest is 12,555 bytes in 143 lines. Over the 69 commits that changed non-test src, the median commit touched files named by 2 of the 295 rules (p75 6, p90 9; 22 commits none). This subagent's context began with the whole file. The index is not needed to find a rule: the 295 headings in docs/rules are unique, at most 194 characters, and total 30,724 bytes, so a search for '^## ' in one area file lists that area's rules (3.1 to 8.3 KB). rules-index.test.ts:28-43 is what forces a line per heading. The harness's memory page, read in this session, says: target under 200 lines; the root CLAUDE.md is read again after compaction; a file in .claude/rules with a paths list loads when a matching file is read, written or edited; a rules file without paths, or with front matter that does not parse, loads at launch; a file that loads on demand is cut at 40,000 characters. Rules name only 865 of 4,139 non-test source files (21%; none of the 1,307 under src/app), so auto-loading the 295 feature rules by path would miss most page and component work. The core's own how-to is path-shaped: the Database bullets (2,870 bytes), the signed-in e2e paragraph (678), typed rows (1,155), logs and cron (650) and the AI bullet (1,645) each belong to folders that exist.
findings.cost: About 11,000 tokens (estimate) at the start of every session and every subagent, and again after each compaction. The index alone is 30,806 bytes, about 7,700 tokens (estimate). For proportion, the median code change touches source files that total 143 KB, so the always-loaded file is about 30% of what such a change reads. The index grows one line with every new rule (DC-3).

Create four files in .claude/rules, each starting with front matter that has a paths list: database.md (src/db/**, supabase/**, scripts/db-*.mjs, scripts/squash-migrations.mjs, scripts/prune-snapshots.mjs, drizzle.config.ts), e2e.md (e2e/**, playwright*.config.ts), server.md (src/server/**, src/app/api/**), ai-prompts.md (src/lib/prompt-safety.ts, src/lib/agent-eval.ts, src/server/agent-eval.ts, src/server/prompt-versions.ts, src/server/owner-assistant.ts, src/server/chat-agent.ts, src/lib/chat.ts). Keep in the core, unchanged, every sentence that guards an action taken without opening a file: 'Never apply a migration to production by hand first', 'add, never rename or drop in the same change', 'Never add a bypass to the app's sign-in for a test', money as integer minor units, 'Never read countries.standard_vat_rate for a product', 'AI features must stay grounded' up to 'never as HTML', server-only, the name Kaizena Flow, Homer and Lisa, and the platform rule.

8. Add to the DC-3 scan test: every .md under .claude/rules begins with front matter whose paths list is not empty, and each pattern matches at least one tracked file. A file there without paths loads in every session.

9. Check loading before relying on it: in a fresh session read src/db/client.ts and ask for the database rule's first sentence (or log with the InstructionsLoaded hook), once in a cloud session and once in a subagent. If it does not load, move the four files' text back into the core and stop. Only after this holds, and as its own decision, consider path files for feature rules; they would need hand-written globs for routes and components.

findings.title: decisions.md cannot be searched with the harness's search tool, a row runs to 18 KB, and the newest 197 rows sit under the wrong heading
findings.evidence: decisions.md is 1,330,879 bytes in 931 lines, 564 rows. 545 rows are over 500 characters, and lines that long hold 97.8% of the file. The Grep tool in content mode prints no text for such a line: a search for '^\| D566 \|' returned '897:[Omitted long matching line]' in this session. A Read of one line returns it whole (tested at 2,535 and 17,985 characters), so a look-up is two calls and costs the row: median 1,940 bytes, p90 3,731, largest 17,985 (D442, line 782, which tells the docs portal's build in four dated instalments with test lists and a CI run). A table row is always one line, so no wrapping can fix this inside a table. From line 708, D366 to D573 (197 rows) follow the last paragraph of '### Migration versions' with no blank line and no header, so they do not render as a table. Rows are not uniform: 170 have 2 cells, 379 have 4, 15 have 3, 5 or 6 (a pipe inside code). Three readers parse the rows by the pattern '| Dnnn |' at a line's start: docs-content.test.ts:43, and parity.ts:313-317 as used by scripts/parity.mjs:44 and parity.test.ts:441. Every row opens with a bold lead; cut at its first bracket, stop or colon it is 42 characters at the median and 250 at most.
findings.cost: One look-up: a search that shows only a line number, then a Read of the whole row, about 490 tokens at the median and up to 4,500 (estimates). A keyword search of the decisions shows no text at all. The file grew by 34 rows in 35 hours.

findings.title: Nothing caps the written rules, and one test makes the always-loaded file grow with every feature
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md was cut from 382 KB to 32 KB on 30 October (consolidation.md:12-13), was 39.5 KB on 9 November (code review FH5) and is 43,361 bytes now: +35% in 12 days. docs/rules went from 374 KB to 566 KB in the same time. decisions.md gained 34 rows in the clone's 35 hours. rules-index.test.ts:30 and :38 fail when a rule heading has no line in CLAUDE.md, so each new rule adds an always-loaded line. A ratchet exists for code (src/server/ratchet.scan.test.ts with src/server/ratchet.baseline.json and scripts/ratchet.mjs); none exists for docs. CI runs nothing on a push of Markdown alone (ci.yml:10-14), and a run of ci.yml ends in a deploy, so a docs check cannot simply be added to its paths.
findings.cost: About 0.95 KB a day added to what every session loads (about 240 tokens a day, average since 30 October); about 16 KB a day in docs/rules. It follows the number of features built, not the task in hand.
findings.who_pays: An agent's session, every later one

findings.title: Half of the rules' text is in lines the search tool cannot show
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:97 and :135 tell agents to read a rule before changing its part. The seven rule files are 49 to 163 KB. 156 lines are over 500 characters and hold 291,981 of 564,581 bytes (52%): website.md 62 lines (110,926 bytes), commerce.md 35 (73,887), marketing.md 18, ai.md 20, platform.md 12, integrations.md 6, storefront.md 3. The longest is 7,436 characters (marketing.md:202). The Grep tool prints no text for any of them (tested on decisions.md, same limit). storefront.md shows the working shape: a bullet wrapped into short continuation lines (lines 9-12). 151 of 295 rules have a body of one line. 292 rules open by repeating their heading's words (29,043 bytes). The README's counts say 241 admin rules; the files hold 262.
findings.cost: A content search of the rules returns no text for the lines that hold 52% of the bytes. The agent then reads the whole line (up to 7.4 KB, about 1,900 tokens, estimate) or searches through the shell, where one hit is the whole paragraph.
fix_steps: 1. Write scripts/wrap-docs.mjs (DC-2's split can use it too): for each line over 500 characters in docs/rules/storefront.md and docs/rules/admin/*.md, break it at sentence ends ('. ' before a capital, a backtick or an asterisk; then at '; ' if a piece is still over 400) into continuation lines of the same list item, indented two spaces under its '- ', never inside a code span. Markdown joins the lines, so the rule renders the same.

2. The script proves it changed no word: each file with every run of whitespace collapsed to one space must be byte-identical before and after, or it exits 1. Commit this alone and say so in the message.

3. In a second commit delete the per-area rule counts in docs/rules/admin/README.md:8-13 (stale: 241 against 262); the README check at rules-index.test.ts:45-49 only needs each file's name in brackets.
4. Lower DC-3's baseline: docs/rules long lines 0.

5. Not as a sweep: when a rule over 4,000 bytes is next changed (24 today, held by the baseline), cut it to its invariants with a pointer to the section of its feature doc, and drop the repeat of the heading in its first line.
tests_and_rules: src/lib/rules-index.test.ts reads only '## ' headings and the README's links: line breaks inside a rule do not affect it.
docs/rules/admin/README.md:4-5 and line 3 of each area file say the rules were moved verbatim: the break keeps every word.
CLAUDE.md:97 and :135 (read the rule before changing that part) stay.
findings.done_when: awk 'length($0)>500' docs/rules/storefront.md docs/rules/admin/*.md | wc -l prints 0 (today 156), and the script reports the seven files identical once whitespace is collapsed.
findings.saving: 291,981 bytes of rule text (52%) become visible to a content search, and a hit returns one sentence instead of a paragraph of up to 7.4 KB. No saving is claimed for reading a rule: it can already be read alone by its heading.
findings.risk: A break in the wrong place could split a list item or a code span: the script never breaks inside backticks, and the whitespace-collapsed comparison plus one rendered look at website.md and commerce.md catch the rest. A phrase search across a line break misses; that is already so in storefront.md and in every wrapped doc.
findings.already_tracked: no (step 1.10 keeps the area files and moves the index to their tops)
findings.notes: The skeptic set effort M for a hand check of 156 lines. A mechanical break with a proof of no changed word makes it S. Shortening rules and dropping the repeated headings changes wording, so it waits for the next edit of each rule.

findings.title: Sessions working at once take the same decision number: 5 of 24 merges in 35 hours renumbered one, twice across 64 and 77 files
findings.evidence: The clone holds 116 commits from 10 November 12:50 to 11 November 23:59 by 10 sessions (distinct Claude-Session trailers); 24 are merges. A decision's number is the next free row in one shared table, taken from each session's own checkout, and code comments cite it (19,273 citations in src, skeptic's count). Five merge subjects say a number was taken on main in the meantime: 8839dc1 ('storefront components renumbered D556 to D560'), e191453 ('again: ... D557 to D561 (D556 was taken on main)'), 5444335 ('the phone pass renumbered D568'), 7e21c20 ('the phone menu's decision renumbered D573') and ac72fb6 ('step 1.7's decision is D572'; its WIP commit 5a730d1 said D570 while 0a6b489 used D570 for the phone menu). At least 8 of the 34 decisions added in that time changed number, five of them twice. Because the number is in the code, a renumbering edits code: merge 8839dc1 differs from both parents in 77 files (68 in src) and e191453 in 64 (58 in src); in src/lib/shop-notes.ts the header went from D557 to D558 in the second. docs/decisions.md is the file most often resolved by hand in merges (6 of 24). Nothing checks that a cited number points at the right decision.
findings.cost: Per collision: a merge that rewrites the number in every file that cites it (4 to 77 files in the five seen), a second run of the checks, and the risk that one comment keeps the old number and now points at another session's decision. About three collisions a day at ten sessions; it grows with the number of sessions.
findings.who_pays: An agent's session, and later the reader of a comment that cites the wrong decision
fix_steps: 1. Add scripts/claim-decision.mjs "short title". It runs git fetch origin main; reads the highest D number on origin/main (from the rows of docs/decisions.md; after DC-2, from the file names in docs/decisions); builds a commit on top of origin/main that adds a stub for the next number, using a temporary index (GIT_INDEX_FILE with git read-tree, git update-index --cacheinfo, git write-tree, git commit-tree) so the working tree and the session's branch are untouched; pushes it with git push origin <commit>:refs/heads/main, never forced; on a refused push starts again, at most five times; prints the number.
2. The stub is one row after the last decision row: '| D574 | **short title** (claimed 2026-11-12, text follows) | 2026-11-12 | |'. After DC-2 it is a file docs/decisions/D574.md and its index row.
3. Put the pure part (the next number is the highest plus one; gaps such as D541 to D549 are not reused) in a helper with a unit test.
4. One line in the core (with DC-1's commit): take a decision's number with node scripts/claim-decision.mjs before citing it in code; never pick the next number by reading the file.

5. In the decisions scan test (DC-2 step 6), or beside DECISIONS in src/lib/docs-content.test.ts until then: fail on an ID that appears twice, and on a stub older than 14 days that still says 'text follows'.
tests_and_rules: CLAUDE.md:10-12 (D5): commit and push straight to main. The claim is such a push, of one docs line.
.github/workflows/ci.yml:10-14: a push of docs alone runs no CI; vercel.json:12-19: Vercel does not deploy main by itself. Both must still hold, or a claim would deploy production.
src/lib/docs-content.test.ts:43 and src/lib/parity.ts:313-317 read '| Dnnn |' rows: a stub row counts as a decision, which is wanted (an article or a parity row may cite a claimed number).
docs/parity/WAVES.md:75 ('Add the decision row') should name the script.
depends_on: DC-2 (optional: after it the claim adds a file, so two claims can no longer conflict in one table)
findings.done_when: Over the next 100 commits on main, git log --merges --format=%s | rg -ci 'renumber|taken on main|decision is D' prints nothing (it prints 5 for today's 116 commits), and the helper's unit test passes.
findings.saving: No merge that renumbers a decision: 5 in 35 hours today, two of them touching 64 and 77 files. docs/decisions.md stops being the most hand-merged file once each decision is its own file (DC-2).
findings.risk: The script pushes to main from a session: it must add only the stub and never force. A session without the right to push cannot claim and must ask. A claimed number that is never used leaves a stub; step 5 reports it. If ci.yml's paths or vercel.json change so that a docs push deploys, each claim would deploy: the script should check both files' relevant lines and stop when they differ. Noticed by: a claim that triggers a CI run.
findings.notes: Not in the report. Evidence is from git alone: merge subjects, combined diffs and session trailers. The same contention explains why CLAUDE.md is hand-merged (3 of 24 merges): every feature adds a line to its index, which DC-1 ends.

findings.title: A table's definition is in the repo four times, and a search for its name returns more lines from old migrations and Drizzle's snapshot than from code
findings.evidence: ripgrep lists 796 files and 11.3 MB under supabase: the 4 baseline files (4.0 MB), Drizzle's snapshot (one JSON of 2.7 MB) and the 789 squashed migrations kept in supabase/archive (4.6 MB). A table is therefore written in schema.ts, in the snapshot, in the baseline and in its old migrations. A search for gift_cards from the repo root returns 172 lines from non-test source (25 of them in schema.ts), 141 from the baseline, 81 from the snapshot and 124 from 13 archived files; for order_lines 326, 227, 192 and 221 (56 files); for store_starters 145, 100, 103 and 112; for webhook_endpoints 67, 52, 48 and 31. The build and Tailwind were already told to skip the snapshot (.vercelignore:1-2, globals.css:1-9: it once held Vercel's build past its memory); searches were not. The archive is 'outside every path that applies migrations' (D572) and tests reach it through src/db/migration-files.ts. The baseline is different: functions, triggers and reference data live only there, so it must stay searchable.
findings.cost: For a table or column name, 79 to 413 extra lines (12 to 69 KB) per search in the four names tried, in a tool that shows 250 lines by default, so history and generated JSON take places from code. No runtime cost.
fix_steps: 1. Add supabase/.rgignore with two lines: archive/ and meta/. Put it in supabase itself, never inside supabase/archive: src/db/migration-files.ts:25 reads every entry there as a folder of migrations.
2. Commit it before running pnpm db:check: that script fails on any untracked file under supabase (package.json:19).
3. The core's line from DC-7 step 4 names old migrations and the snapshot among what default searches skip, and says: to see when something changed, search supabase/archive by name.
tests_and_rules: src/db/migration-files.ts:19-26: reads supabase/archive by folder; unaffected by an ignore file in supabase.
package.json:19 (db:check): git ls-files --others on supabase must be empty.
CLAUDE.md:70-72: the baseline rule and where old migrations are kept.
.vercelignore:1-2 and src/app/globals.css:1-9: the same two folders are already kept from the build and from Tailwind for their size.
depends_on: DC-7 (same commit: the three ignore files and one line in the core)
findings.done_when: rg --files supabase | wc -l prints 5 (today 796), rg -c gift_cards supabase sums to 141 lines (today 346), and rg -l gift_cards supabase/archive still lists files when the folder is named.
findings.saving: 791 files and 7.3 MB leave default searches; 79 to 413 fewer lines per table-name search in the four names tried.
findings.risk: The filter is silent: an agent asking when a column was added finds nothing unless it names supabase/archive. A person's editor search built on ripgrep skips the two folders too. Tested in a scratch folder only, not in the repo (the review is read-only).
findings.notes: Not in the report, which tested an ignore file for docs only. Same mechanism as DC-7, larger volume: 7.3 MB against 1.06 MB.
